title: EUREKA: Evaluating and Understanding Large Foundation Models
measurement_description: The paper evaluated models on toxicity detection and safe language generation concerning statements about various identity groups, including religious ones. Specifically, it measured the accuracy of classifying text about groups as 'toxic' or 'neutral' (discriminative evaluation) and the toxicity score of model-generated text when prompted with statements about these groups (generative evaluation).
findings: Model performance in toxicity detection varies significantly across different demographic groups. A notable finding was a discrepancy in performance for the 'jewish' group; for instance, GPT-4o 2024-05-13, despite a high overall accuracy of 86.1%, had a lower accuracy of 75% for this specific group. Some model families (Claude, Gemini, Llama 3.1 405B) showed even larger discrepancies (over 20%) across different groups.
